title.narrative: Protection anticipatory actions in Afmadow, Xudur, Qansax Dheere,Dinsor & Baidoa.

description.narrative: Below normal rains driven by La Nina condition are projected to happen between November to January 2025. These conditions are expected to worsen crop and fodder production – particularly in locations dependent on rainfed agriculture and pastoralist activities. Food insecurity complicates and exacerbates existing vulnerabilities and reinforces social divisions already created by chronic conflict. Direct and indirect climate impacts disproportionately affect girls and women, who are more likely to forgo education, engage in risky coping mechanisms, and be exposed to gender-based violence as a result. Youth are also put at risk by climate-related displacement, and the resulting hopelessness and marginalization among young men can in turn help fuel conflict. As part of its protection response, UNHCR will target 15,000 individuals. The response consists of the establishment of Protection desks for the provision of quality specialized protection services including Protection monitoring, case management and referrals (Protection, CP, GBV), feedback mechanism, psycho-social support, and Individual Protection Assistance (IPA) in both, areas of origin affected by drought and areas affected by drought related newly displacements. The protection response will also activate a Fast-track referral mechanism (FTRM). The FTRM is a joint Food Security (FS), CCCM and Protection initiative for identification and fast-track protection-related referrals for inclusion of minorities and other marginalized groups into the food security response.Protection of civilians’ response will target the areas of displacement as well as areas of origin through two parallel workstreams focusing on a) Community-Based Protection in Hard-to-Reach areas (Community-led Protection and Community-Based Child Protection and GBV initiatives), and b) support the inter-sectoral coordination and response through Conflict Sensitivity Analysis in the three prioritized districts (Afmadow, Baydhaba and Diinsor).The Protection and GBV AoR responses are designed to complement each other under this CERF allocation The Protection response will enhance outreach to priority areas -including Hard-to-Reach- through the Protection Desks response ensuring a holistic availability of protection services to the affected population. The Protection Desks response will include the identification and referral vulnerable populations to specialized services and humanitarian support. Some of these cases identified through the Protection Desks will be referred to the GBV AoR response which focus on the provision of dignity and hygiene kits, and specialized services through the Women and Girls Safe Spaces (WGSS) and GBV One-Stop Centers (OSC). Moreover, in support of the Protection Desks response, GBV AoR will provide updated service mapping and referral pathways for the priority districts which will be operationally used by the Protection Desk teams as well as disseminated within the affected communities
